newsitem.title: UK: World crude tanker rates seen strong into 1997.
newsitem.headline: World crude tanker rates seen strong into 1997.

text.p: The cost of chartering a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) could rise next year as demand for vessels improves and the size of the fleet remains broadly static, shipping brokers Jacobs & Partners Ltd said on Tuesday.

"With a relatively stable fleet size and some additional VLCC demand likely to be forthcoming we remain confident that freight rates will be at least as firm as the current year," said Jacobs in its World Tanker Fleet Review.

Strong freight rates so far this year encouraged owners to keep older vessels in service -- only seven VLCCs built in the mid 1970s were scrapped in the first half of 1996 against 21 in the same period of 1995 -- earning in excess of $25,000 per day after running costs.

But even if demolition remains an unattractive option -- at the current rate it would take 15 years to scrap the remaining mid 1970s tonnage -- the size of the VLCC fleet will be little changed next year despite new building, Jacobs said.

"Although this analysis suggests that the change to the VLCC fleet during 1997 could range between plus or minus two million deadweight tonnes, the most likely outcome is a marginal decline," the broker's review said.
Extra demand for tonnage would come from growing world oil consumption and the return of Iraq to the spot crude market for the first time since the Gulf War.
"The outlook for VLCC demand over the remainder of 1996 and throughout 1997 does look quite encouraging," said Jacobs.

Forecasts of rising production in the North Sea, Latin America, Asia and Australia and West Africa should also give owners of medium-sized Aframax and Suezmax carriers cause for encouragement, they added.
"There do seem to be some cautious grounds for optimism for medium crude carriers during the next 18 months," Jacobs said.
